body_ar: "التاسعة عشرة قوله لأعطين الراية" غدا رجلا يحب الله ورسوله ويحبه الله ورسوله يفتح الله على يديه "علم من أعلام النبوة" ودليل من دلائلها لأنه قد فتح الله على يديه فحقق الله ما أخبر به رسوله (ص) فكان ذلك معجزة للنبي (ص)، "العشرون تفله في عينيه علم من أعلامها أيضا" أي برؤه بتفله في عينيه علم من أعلام النبوة فذلك دليل واضح على بركته (ص)، "الحادية والعشرون فضيلة علي رضي الله عنه" فإن النبي (ص) أعلن هذا للناس من قبل، وأتى به بهذا الأسلوب الذي يقتضي أن يحرصوا على التنافس فيه وأن يهتموا به ..
body_en: 'Nineteenth: his saying, "I shall certainly give the banner"' — tomorrow — 'to a man who loves God and His Messenger and whom God and His Messenger love; God will grant victory at his hands' — 'is one of the signs of prophethood', and one of its proofs, because God did grant victory at his hands, so God brought about what His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, had announced, and that was an evidentiary miracle (muʿjizah) for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. 'Twentieth: his spitting into his eyes is likewise one of its signs' — that is, his being cured by the Prophet's spittle applied to his eyes is one of the signs of prophethood, and that is a clear proof of his blessedness, may God bless him and grant him peace. 'Twenty-first: the merit of Ali, may God be pleased with him' — for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, announced this to the people beforehand, and presented it in a manner calculated to make them eager to compete for it and to attach importance to it ..

options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.

The numbered items are the 'points of benefit' (masāʾil) appended to a chapter of the base text; the quotation marks marking them are in the Arabic source and have been kept. The word غدا ('tomorrow') falls outside the source's quotation marks although it belongs to the hadith; the English reproduces the source's punctuation rather than correcting it.
The trailing '..' is in the Arabic source and marks where the written excerpt stops.
